seoTitle: Seinfeld Test: Which Character Are You? (12 Questions)
metaDescription: Take the Seinfeld test: 12 everyday questions reveal whether you're Jerry, George, Elaine, Kramer, Newman, Frank Costanza, Puddy or J. Peterman — with your full character breakdown.
intro: Are you the observer, the schemer, or the one who walks in without knocking? Answer 12 everyday questions about friends, neighbours and life's little annoyances, and find out which Seinfeld character you are.

characters.name: Jerry Seinfeld
characters.title: The Observer
characters.summary: Clever, picky and always watching. You notice every tiny flaw, and you can make a joke out of any of them.
description: Like Jerry, you notice everything. He's a stand-up comedian who turns everyday annoyances into material.
You're very hard to please. Jerry dumps women over the smallest things, like a laugh he can't stand or hands he thinks are too big.
You like what you like. Jerry's life revolves around Superman and cereal, and he greets his nemesis with a very cold 'Hello, Newman'.
characters.flaw: You find a reason to walk away from anything that gets too serious.
characters.signature: A spotless apartment, a shelf of cereal and a Superman figure in the corner.
characters.clashReason: they'd find the one thing wrong with you, and never stop mentioning it

characters.name: George Costanza
characters.title: The Schemer
characters.summary: Anxious, cheap and endlessly creative with the truth. You'll do almost anything to avoid doing actual work.
description: Like George, you can talk your way into anything. His favourite fake identity is Art Vandelay, an architect who doesn't exist.
You worry about everything. George is insecure about his looks, his job and his love life, usually all at once.
Sometimes doing the opposite works. In 'The Opposite', George does the exact opposite of what his instincts tell him, and he lands a job with the New York Yankees.
characters.flaw: You'll put more effort into avoiding work than the work itself would take.
characters.signature: A fake job title, a lie that's got out of hand and an excuse for everything.
characters.clashReason: they'd lie to get out of plans with you, then lie about the lie

characters.name: Elaine Benes
characters.title: The Straight Talker
characters.summary: Smart, blunt and nobody's pushover. You say exactly what you think, and you don't care who's watching.
description: Like Elaine, you're nobody's fool. She works at Pendant Publishing, then for the eccentric J. Peterman.
You commit, even when you shouldn't. Elaine's dancing in 'The Little Kicks' is so bad that George calls it a full-body dry heave set to music.
You keep going back to the same mistakes. Elaine can't seem to stay away from her on-off boyfriend, Puddy.
characters.flaw: You judge people harshly, then end up doing exactly what they did.
characters.signature: A big handbag, a sharp comeback and dance moves nobody can unsee.
characters.clashReason: they'd tell you exactly what's wrong with your outfit, your partner and your plan

characters.name: Kramer
characters.title: The Wild Card
characters.summary: Spontaneous, confident and full of strange ideas. You walk into every room like you own it.
description: Like Kramer, you make an entrance. He's Jerry's neighbour, and he slides through Jerry's door without ever knocking.
You've always got a new business idea. Kramer runs Kramerica Industries, and he once pitched a coffee table book about coffee tables.
Nothing fazes you. However strange the plan, Kramer goes all in, and every so often it actually works.
characters.flaw: You act first, think later, and borrow everything in between.
characters.signature: A vintage shirt, a wild new invention and a friend's front door that never seems to be locked.
characters.clashReason: they'd walk into your home without knocking and eat your food

characters.name: Newman
characters.title: The Nemesis
characters.summary: Petty, dramatic and surprisingly clever. You never forget a slight, and you always have a scheme going.
description: Like Newman, you know how to hold a grudge. He's a postal worker and Jerry's arch-enemy.
You make everything sound dramatic. Newman uses big words, writes poetry and gets hysterical when things go wrong.
You have a soft spot you'd never show Jerry. Newman has an unrequited crush on Elaine.
characters.flaw: You'd rather win a petty feud than be happy.
characters.signature: A postal uniform, a long-running grudge and a very dramatic 'Hello, Jerry'.
characters.clashReason: they'd turn the smallest disagreement into a years-long feud

characters.name: Frank Costanza
characters.title: The Hothead
characters.summary: Loud, stubborn and absolutely sure of himself. You live by your own rules, and you'll shout to defend them.
description: Like Frank, you have a temper. He's George's father, and he goes from calm to shouting in seconds.
You make your own traditions. Frank invented Festivus, his own holiday, complete with the airing of grievances.
You try to stay calm, loudly. Frank's tape tells him to say 'Serenity now!' whenever he gets angry, and he shouts it.
characters.flaw: You lose your temper first and find out what happened later.
characters.signature: A bare aluminium pole, a list of grievances and a very loud 'Serenity now!'.
characters.clashReason: they'd air every grievance they've ever had with you, out loud, at dinner

characters.name: David Puddy
characters.title: The Unbothered One
characters.summary: Calm, simple and impossible to rattle. Drama happens around you, never to you.
description: Like Puddy, nothing gets under your skin. He's Elaine's on-off boyfriend, and he stays calm whatever she throws at him.
You don't waste words. Puddy's answer to most things is 'Yeah, that's right.'
You're good with your hands. Puddy used to be a mechanic.
characters.flaw: You're so relaxed that people can't tell whether you care.
characters.signature: A squint, a shrug and a 'Yeah, that's right.'
characters.clashReason: they'd stay completely calm while you were losing your mind

characters.name: J. Peterman
characters.title: The Adventurer
characters.summary: Eccentric, dramatic and full of stories. You turn every ordinary moment into an epic tale.
description: Like J. Peterman, you've got a story for everything. He runs a clothing catalogue, and every item comes with a tale of adventure.
You live life like a novel. Peterman is an eccentric explorer type who talks about the world in grand, dramatic sentences.
You're a memorable boss. Peterman is Elaine's boss in the show's final seasons, and working for him is never boring.
characters.flaw: You make a simple story so long that people forget what the question was.
characters.signature: A catalogue full of adventures, a tale from a far-off land and a very dramatic pause.
characters.clashReason: they'd answer a simple question with a twenty-minute story

questions.text: Someone you're dating has one tiny annoying habit. You...

options.text: Can't stop noticing it. It might be a deal-breaker
Stay. You're lucky anyone's dating you at all
Make a face every time they do it, and hope they notice
Don't notice. You're pretty easygoing

questions.text: A friend asks to borrow some money. You...

options.text: Come up with a very detailed reason why now is a bad time
Lend it, then bring it up every time you see them
Offer them a share in your latest business idea instead
Hand it over with a grand gesture, as if you're saving their life
A diner, a few laughs and a bowl of cereal at midnight
Fixing up your car, then a long nap
An adventure somewhere far away, with a great story at the end
Whatever plan you came up with at 2am

questions.text: Someone cuts in front of you in a queue. You...

options.text: Explode. Loudly. Everyone needs to hear this
Tell them exactly what you think, and enjoy every second
Make a sarcastic comment to the person next to you
Make a speech about everything that's wrong with society

questions.text: Your boss asks you to work late on a Friday. You...

options.text: Stay, and spend the evening looking busy rather than being busy
Say no. You've had plans for weeks
Agree, then do as little as humanly possible
Shrug, stay, and fix the office printer while you're at it

questions.text: The holidays are coming up. You...

options.text: Refuse to do the usual thing. You'll make up your own holiday instead
Buy everyone a gift that's slightly cheaper than the one they got you
Write a dramatic description of each gift on the label
Turn up with a strange homemade gift nobody asked for

questions.text: A friend says their new partner is perfect. You...

options.text: Spot the one flaw within five minutes
Nod. Sounds good to you
Ask a lot of pointed questions about them
Get a bit jealous, then a bit competitive

questions.text: Your neighbour is someone you can't stand. You...

options.text: Greet them politely, in a tone that says exactly how you feel
Spend months trying to catch them out
Become best friends with them. Why not?
Air every grievance you have with them at dinner, one by one

questions.text: You come up with a business idea. You...

options.text: Launch it tomorrow. Who needs a plan?
Pitch it with a dramatic story about where the idea came from
Get excited, then give up the moment it needs real work
Get someone else to do the work, and take half the money

questions.text: The dancing starts at a wedding. You...

options.text: Dance like nobody's watching. Everybody is
Stay at your table and make jokes about everyone who's dancing
Dance, with a completely straight face
Go and complain to the DJ about the music

questions.text: You live in a New York apartment building, and your neighbour keeps walking in without knocking. You...

options.text: Don't mind at all. Offer them a drink
Make a house rule about it, and enforce it loudly
Start walking into their place without knocking too
Raid their fridge right back. Fair is fair

questions.text: You and your friends end up in court for something you all did together. You...

options.text: Give a grand, dramatic speech in your own defence
Relax. Jail sounds like a bit of an adventure
Refuse to cooperate on principle, whatever it costs you
Panic, then try to lie your way out of it
